//: What apps/demo is built to produce. tests/e2e/scan.e2e.test.ts reads this file, so a defect that stops being detected fails the build rather than quietly disappearing from the output.

mustFail.23a2a8: informative img with no alt attribute
mustFail.24afc2: letter-spacing under 0.12em marked important in a style attribute
mustFail.46ca7f: role=presentation on an element that tabindex puts in the focus order
mustFail.5c01ea: aria-checked on a link, where it is not permitted
mustFail.5f99a7: aria-labeledby, which is not an ARIA attribute
mustFail.6cfa84: aria-hidden container with a focusable link inside it
mustFail.7d6734: svg role=img with no accessible name
mustFail.8fc3b6: object rendering non-text content with no accessible name
mustFail.97a4e1: button whose only content is an icon glyph
mustFail.afw4f7: grey on white below the contrast floor
mustFail.b5c3f8: html element with no lang attribute
mustFail.bc659a: meta refresh with a 30 second delay
mustFail.bf051a: lang="engRish", which is not a language tag
mustFail.bisz58: the same refresh, under the rule that allows no exception
mustFail.c487ae: link whose only content is an image with an empty alt
mustFail.e086e5: placeholder used as a label, and a label whose for names no id

mustNotEvaluate.09o5cg: enhanced contrast needs layout and paint, and the static renderer has neither
mustNotEvaluate.afw4f7: minimum contrast, same reason. It appears in mustFail as well because a peer engine reports it from the declared colours and the invariant forces that through

cannotDetect.//: Defects that are in the markup and that Marlo does not report. Listed here rather than removed from the page, because an undetected defect that nobody wrote down looks exactly like a defect that is not there.
cannotDetect.e6952f: The page has name="city" name="town" on one input. Every HTML parser drops the second attribute before any DOM exists, so a DOM-based check cannot see it. Detecting this needs the source bytes, which arrive with the repair layer.
cannotDetect.9eb3f6: The page has alt="IMG_20240117_cart.png" matching its own src. Marlo returns cantTell rather than failed, because deciding that a name is a filename rather than a description is a judgment it is not confident enough to make. That caution is why its recall on the naming rules is below its peers'.
cannotDetect.e88epe: aria-hidden on an image with meaningful alt text. Marlo answers cantTell by design: whether the image is decorative is a question about intent, and the rule is advisory for that reason.
